newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil air force plane crashes in sea, kills one.
newsitem.headline: Brazil air force plane crashes in sea, kills one.

text.p: A Brazilian air force plane lost a wing in mid-flight during an air show and crashed into the ocean on Saturday off Brazil's southern coast, killing one person on a nearby beach and injuring five, authorities said.
A police spokeswoman in the port of Sao Vicente said a 16-year-old boy was killed and five people injured when debris from the plane fell on Gonzaga beach, 40 miles (60 km) east of Sao Paulo.
Air force spokesman said the pilot of the T-27 Tucano, of the elite Smoke Squadron, ejected safely and was plucked from the Atlantic Ocean by rescuers, shaken but unhurt.
"The pilot is resting in hospital. He's doing well," he said.

Brazilian television showed dramatic footage of the plane's right wing tearing away as it performed a steep climb. The pilot managed to stabilise the plane briefly before it nosedived. He ejected seconds before it slammed into the sea.
"An investigation has already begun," the air force spokesman said.
The crash occurred at the end of an airshow that was part of the air force's Wing Week festivities.
